Mr. Sanpreet Singh Ajmani, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State/respondent no.1.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Advocate for H.N.B. Garhwal University, Srinagar, Garhwal.
Dated: August 1, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Counter affidavits, in all the petitions, filed on
behalf of H.N.B. Garhwal University, Sri Nagar, Garhwal
in the Court today. Same are taken on record. The
petitioner counsel states that he would not file any
rejoinder affidavit. Counsel for the parties agree that the
writ petitions may be heard and decided today itself.

3
2. Parties in all the petitions, except petitioners are
same. Controversy involved in all the petitions is same,
therefore, all the petitions have been consolidated and are
being decided by a common judgment. Writ Petition No.
2776 of 2011 (M/S) shall be the leading case.
3. The petitioners, in all petitions, have prayed for the
following reliefs:-
"A. To issue appropriate writ, order or
direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent no.5 to register
the petitioner in the roll list of
Uttarakhand Nursing Council and allot
the RNRM Certificate (i.e. registered
nurse and registered midwife) without
causing any further delay.
B. To issue appropriate writ, order or
direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent no.1-i the
District Magistrate to take appropriate
action against the respondent no.3 i.e.
the Director of the Institute.
C. Cost of the petition be also awarded.
D. To issue any other order, writ or
direction which this Hon'ble Court may
deem fit and proper in the facts and
circumstances of the case."
4. All these writ petitions were filed in the year 2011.
On 09.01.2012 a common order was passed in all the
petitions directing the Secretary, Health and Education,
Government of Uttarakhand, Dehradun to personally look
into the matter, as the petitioners had informed that in
many other cases, by a late registration fee, the institute
had been registered with the Uttarakhand Nursing
Council. This Court further observed that if any such
avenues are possible under the law, the Secretary, Health
and Education, Govt. of Uttarakhand shall also pass a

4
speaking order on the representations of the petitioners
as early as possible.
5. Thereafter, the representations of the petitioners
were rejected.
6. On 22nd February, 2012 notices were issued to the
respondent nos. 2, 3, 4, 5 and & 7. On 17.03.2012, office
has reported that though notices were issued to these
respondents by registered post on 06.03.2012, but neither
undelivered envelopes were returned back, nor anyone
filed Vakalatnama on behalf of these respondents. In
every petition, the office reported the said endorsement.
In Writ Petition No. 2771/2011 the respondent no.2 put in
appearance through an Advocate and has also filed
counter affidavit.
7. Considering the fact that undelivered envelopes
have not returned back, service upon respondent nos. 2,
3, 4, 5 & 7 is found sufficient.
8. Precisely stated that the respondent no.2, namely
Narayan Swami Hospital and Dental College, Dehradun
(hereinafter referred to as the 'Institute') represented
itself that it is affiliated to the H.N.B. Garhwal University,
Sri Nagar (for short the University) and is approved by the
Indian Nursing Council, New Delhi and has obtained
approval from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
and Department of Higher Education, State Technical
Board, Govt. of Uttarakhand and National Council for
Teachers Education, New Delhi. It has also obtained 'No
Objection Certificate' for running the 'Institute' and
various courses, including B.Sc. (Nursing) 4 years course.

5
It was also envisaged at page 13 of the prospectus, issued
by the 'Institute', that the 'Institute' has been allotted 30
seats in respect of B.Sc. (Nursing) 4 years course by the
University and Govt. of Uttarakhand/Councils/Boards. In
the year 2006, 11 candidates, the petitioners, joined the
'Institute' for pursuing B.Sc. (Nursing) 4 years course. The
petitioners successfully completed their B.Sc. (Nursing) 4
years course in the year 2011 and were awarded the final
year marks sheet on 22nd January, 2011 and provisional
certificate on 20th August, 2011 by the University. As is
requirement, the students have to apply for registration of
their names with the Uttarakhand Nursing Council
without which the students cannot even apply for job in
any sector i.e. private or Government. Now the petitioners
cannot even apply in any institution for higher studies in
India or abroad without registration in Uttarakhand
Nursing Council.
9. It is further asserted that after receiving the
provisional certificate of the said course, the petitioners
approached Uttarakhand Nursing Council, Dehradun
alongwith the bank draft of ` 500/- in favour of the
Registrar, Uttarakhand Nursing Council, Dehradun for
registration of their names, but they were shocked when
they were refused, even to issue the Form for seeking
registration for the reason that the 'Institute' is not
registered in its office. The petitioners were also informed
that the 'Institute' has not applied for and did not
complete the required formalities for seeking registration
in the Uttarakhand Nursing Council, Dehradun.
10. On refusal to issue the Form for registration, even
by the Uttarakhand Nursing Council, the petitioners,

6
alongwith their parents, approached the 'Institute', where
they were informed that the 'Institute' has already
requested to the Minister of Health Education, Govt. of
Uttarakhand, Dehradun, who has been pleased to direct
the Registrar, Uttarakhand Nursing Council to take action
for registration of the 'Institute', as per the rules.
Thereafter, the petitioners represented the matter to
various authorities, including the Director of the
'Institute', through his counsel, calling upon the
respondents to take action in the matter but nothing was
done. The petitioners also sought information under
Section 7 of the Right to Information Act and when no
information was supplied, the petitioners preferred
appeal under RTI Act. On the directions issued by the
Appellate Authority, the Registrar, Uttarakhand Nursing
Council, Dehradun provided the required information
vide reply dated 19.11.2011. By the said reply, it was
informed by the Registrar, Uttarakhand Nursing Council,
Dehradun that the 'Institute' is not registered with it and
it has sent the letters to the 'Institute' calling upon to get
the inspection of the Nursing College done. It was also
informed that for nursing jobs, the registration is
necessary and it has not granted the permission to run the
B.Sc. (Nursing) Course. It was also informed that as the
'Institute' is not registered with it, the registration of the
students, who have pursued the same course, cannot be
registered with it. Being aggrieved, the petitioners were
constrained to file these petitions.
11. On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel for the
State referred paragraph no.6 of the counter affidavit filed
on behalf of State as well as Uttarakhand Nursing Council.
In their counter affidavits, these respondents have come

7
up with the case that the State Government vide letter
dated 9th October, 2006 granted 'No Objection Certificate'
(NOC) in favour of the 'Institute' with the condition that
the said 'Institute' should obtain approval from Bhartiya
Nursing Parishad, New Delhi and comply with the
directions/ guidelines issued by the Indian Nursing
Council from time to time. In furtherance, the Indian
Nursing Council inspected the said 'Institute' on
19/20.06.2007 and accorded approval in favour of the
Institute, vide letter dated 10.08.2007 for the session
2007-08.
12. These respondents also asserted that the petitioners
managed to get admission in the said 'Institute' in the
academic session 2006-07. It is also submitted that it is
clear that the petitioners had taken admission in the
'Institute' prior to grant of 'No Objection Certificate' by
the State Government of Uttarakhand and the approval
accorded by the Indian Nursing Council. It is also stated
that since the petitioners got admission in the 'Institute'
in the academic session 2006-07, and by that time, no
approval was accorded by the Indian Nursing Council in
favour of the 'Institute', therefore, the question regarding
registration of the petitioners by the Uttarakhand State
Nursing Council does not arise because the approval of
the State Nursing Council is to be accorded after the
approval of the Indian Nursing Council.
13. It is further asserted that Indian Nursing Council
accorded its approval in favour of the 'Institute' for the
academic session 2007-08 with the condition that
necessary approval of the Uttarakhand State Nursing
Council should have been accorded, but inspite of the

8
instruction of the Indian Nursing Council, the 'Institute'
never sought approval from the Uttarakhand State
Nursing Council, nor the same was accorded in favour of
the 'Institute'. It is lastly asserted that the Uttarakhand
State Nursing Council, Dehradun never accorded any
approval or sanction in favour of the 'Institute'.
14. Thus, the only objection raised by the respondents
is that the 'Institute' was not accorded approval for the
session 2006-07 and the NOC was granted to the
'Institute' for the session 2007-08. On the basis of these
assertion, learned Standing Counsel for the State argued
that in such circumstances, the petitions lack merit and
deserve to be dismissed.
15. Mr. Paresh Tripathi, learned counsel for the
University submitted that the 'Institute' applied for
affiliation with the University on 01.05.2006 and the
University nominated its inspection team on 02.05.2006
and the inspection was conducted on 11.05.2006 and after
the inspection, University recommended for provisional
affiliation with the intake of 30 students for B.Sc. Nursing
Course. He then submitted that since NOC was given in
favour of the 'Institute' from the State of Uttarakhand,
vide its letter dated 09.10.2006 granting the conditional
No Objection for running the B.Sc. Nursing and Midwife
Course, the petitioners were permitted to appear in
examination. He submitted that, however the University
never granted any approval or affiliation to the 'Institute',
but since 'No Objection Certificate' was given by the State
Government, the petitioners were permitted to appear in
the examination and their result was declared.

9
16. I have considered the submissions of the learned
counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire
record. Though, it is true that the students were admitted
for the academic session 2006-07 without grant of
approval. It is also true that for the academic session
2006-07 'No Objection Certificate' was given by the State
Government in favour of the 'Institute', simultaneously it
is also true that the University considered the NOC given
by the State Government on 09.10.2006, and under the
directions of State Government issued vide letters dated
03.04.2008, 21.10.2008, 08.04.2009 and 15.04.2010, as
mentioned in the counter affidavit of the University, the
University permitted the petitioners to appear in the
examination, but factual position is that the petitioners
have undergone B.Sc. Nursing Course and have also got
degree from the University. The petitioners took
admission in the institute on the basis of information
given by respondent nos. 2 & 3, and on the basis of
prospectus supplied by the 'Institute' to the students/
petitioners and applied for B.Sc. Nursing Course, thus
there was no occasion for them to suspect the genuineness
of the 'Institute', as the petitioners were being permitted
to appear in the examination and their result was declared
on yearly basis and the degree was also issued by the
University, the genuineness of which has not been
doubted even by the respondents.
17. In the case in hand, admittedly all the respondents
have committed mistake. Consequent upon such mistake
committed by the State Government as well as the
University, the 'Institute' permitted the petitioners to
pursue their course without verifying the fact that the
'Institute' is having approval from the competent

10
authority. The respondent nos. 2 & 3 have committed
explicit blunder, in fact, they played with the career of the
petitioners as well as the institute. Moreover, the
'Institute', without obtaining permission from the
Authority Competent and without getting the 'Institute'
affiliated with the H.N.B. Garwal University, Pauri
Garhwal, admitted the petitioners, took huge amount as
fee and the petitioners were kept in dark that at the time
of admission neither there was any approval from the
Indian Nursing Council nor there was any affiliation with
the Garhwal University. Students believed on the
information given in the prospectus. In such
circumstances, it is held that the petitioners cannot be
blamed and should not be punished, in any manner for no
fault of their. Therefore, in the peculiar circumstances of
the case, the writ petitions deserve to be allowed.
18. For the preceding reasons, the writ petitions are
allowed. Uttarakhand Nursing Council, Dehradun is
directed to enroll the petitioners and register them in the
roll list of Uttarakhand Nursing Council and allot the
RNRM Certificate expeditiously, but not later than one
month, from the date of production of a certified copy of
this order. So far as relief No. (B) made in the prayer
clause of the writ petition, this Court is refraining from
passing any order and it is open for the petitioners to
approach the appropriate forum for redressal of their
grievances, if any. Though, respondent no.2 (Naryan
Swami Hospital and Dental College, Dehradun) and
respondent no.3 (Manish Verma) are solely responsible
for the harassment caused to the petitioners and I was
inclined to impose heavy cost on them, but with great

11
effort, I prevented myself from imposing heavy cost on
them.
19. All pending applications also stand disposed of.
20. Let certified copy of the judgment be placed in the
connected writ petitions.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 01.08.2013
